editions.text:
The station's busiest day in the past week recorded 142 feeder visits and 15 species, far exceeding the recent average of roughly 51 visits. Tufted Titmice dominated the visual log with 70 confident sightings, opening and closing the day's activity, while Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays led the auditory count. This activity level aligns with the addition of a new tube seed feeder installed on the left hook of the pole earlier in the week.

The 06:52 switch to the new microphone source captures the station's full auditory range, including first-time detections for Carolina Chickadees, House Finches, Northern Mockingbirds, and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds. These species were already known to the area but had not been reliably identified by the previous audio system. The new source also records the first confident visual sightings of Gray Catbirds and House Finches at this station.

Regulars such as Carolina Wrens, Eastern Towhees, and American Crows held steady throughout the day, with Crows showing a noticeable increase in evening activity. No new station changes occurred after the morning audio upgrade and the afternoon seed feeder replacement.

The day opened with a Blue Jay landing thirteen minutes after sunrise, soon joined by a steady stream of Tufted Titmice that anchored the morning's activity. By 8:00, the feeder had settled into a busy rhythm, with Carolina Chickadees and Titmice sharing the tube seed feeder while Carolina Wrens dominated the background noise. The auditory count swelled significantly in the 8:00 and 9:00 hours, driven largely by Wren detections.

A mix of Mourning Doves and White-breasted Nuthatches worked the feeders, punctuated by the call of a Red-shouldered Hawk. The activity level far outpaces the recent daily averages, with 156 feeder visits and 15 species recorded by 10:30. A Tufted Titmouse was the last confirmed visual before the cutoff.

The Carolina Wren's vocal dominance fades, replaced by Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays. Tufted Titmice remain the primary visual fixture, with ninety-four confident visits anchoring the feeder activity. The weather holds steady at a high of 29.4 C with light winds and no precipitation.

Current totals show 217 feeder visits and 15 species, exceeding the recent daily average of roughly 52 visits by this time. A Carolina Chickadee perched on the tube seed feeder, while a Blue Jay was noted on the ground near the red nectar source. The last confirmed visual was a Tufted Titmouse.

The day closes with 232 feeder visits and 16 species. The final hours saw a distinct shift in the auditory landscape. Northern Cardinals and Carolina Wrens reasserted their presence in the 19:00 hour.

As dusk approached, the visual log ended with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at sunset, marking the station's last confirmed visitor. This hummingbird was one of only two seen today, alongside a pair of Gray Catbirds whose presence remained probable. The steady weather, with highs near 30 C and light winds, offered a constant backdrop.

In the final minute before dark, a Northern Mockingbird and a Black-crowned Night Heron added their calls to the fading light.
